EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  
“How much of the well-known patterns that (i) interventions look smaller in later
grades and (ii) early-grade gains ‘fade out’ is simply a consequence of the way
achievement is scaled?”

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Method: Difference-in-Differences (with an event–study extension).

Rationale  
• The two statewide “test edition” changes in North Carolina in spring 2001
  and spring 2006 are plausibly exogenous to any one cohort.  
• A new test edition mechanically re-sets item difficulty and score scaling.
  If the regularities above are partly a scaling artifact, the magnitude of
  (a) cross-grade persistence of a fixed underlying skill and (b) the
  contemporaneous payoff to the same underlying skill should jump exactly in
  the cohorts first exposed to the new edition.  
• Grades that normally display the strongest widening of the knowledge
  distribution (6–8) should react the most to the re-scaling, whereas grades
  3–5 serve as an internal benchmark.  
• A DID that compares (Later-grade – Early-grade) differences before vs. after
  a test redesign therefore isolates the “pure measurement” component.

Equation (cohort × grade cell as the unit of observation)

        β_gct  = θ + δ · Post_t × Upper_g + γ_g + λ_t + ε_gct      (1)

β_gct  : estimated slope from a first-stage regression of math score on an
         invariant proxy for underlying knowledge (college going or baseline PIAT).
Post_t : indicator that cohort c in test year t faced a new edition (2001, 2006).  
Upper_g: 1 for grades 6–8, 0 for grades 3–5.  
δ       : causal effect of re-scaling on the measured payoff to a
         fixed amount of knowledge in upper relative to lower grades.

An event-study version replaces Post_t with a full set of leads/lags to check
pre-trends.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable            : Exposure to a newly introduced EOG math test
                                 edition (Test2001, Test2006).  

Control group                 : Cohorts sitting for the previous test version
                                 (pre-2001 or pre-2006).  

Treatment timing              : Spring 2001 for edition change #1;
                                 spring 2006 for edition change #2.
                                 Treated from the first spring in which the
                                 revised exam is administered.  

Within-cohort contrast (Upper vs. Lower grades) supplies the second
difference that nets out any level shifts common to all grades.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of a test redesign, the gap in the
    knowledge-to-score slope between upper and lower grades would have evolved
    smoothly.  
    • Plausibility: No curriculum or accountability shock coincides exactly
      with both redesign years in CMS; reading tests (placebo) provide a check.

A2. Exogeneity of edition timing: Test-development calendar is driven by state
    psychometric requirements and not by unobserved changes in student ability.  
    • Plausibility: Edition years were set years in advance; no sudden district
      initiative in 2001 or 2006 targeted specific grades.

A3. Stable mapping from underlying knowledge to the proxy (college going).  
    • Plausibility: College-attendance behavior does not shift exactly in 2001
      or 2006 for elementary cohorts, and any slow secular change is differenced out.

A4. No structural break in variance of underlying knowledge exactly in those
    years.  
    • Plausibility: Cohort size and composition evolve smoothly; large CMS
      desegregation ruling is in 2002—will be explicitly checked.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & REMEDIES  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Simultaneous policy change (e.g., end of court-ordered busing in 2002)
    correlated with the 2001 redesign.  
    Remedy:  
       • Triple-difference: include reading score slopes as an additional
         untreated subject.  
       • Cohort fixed effects and event-study plots to test for breaks exactly
         in 2002.

T2. Demographic composition shifts (racial re-sorting, in-/out-migration).  
    Remedy:  
       • Control for cohort-grade means of FRL status, race, and LEP share.  
       • Weight cell-level regressions by cohort size; show that results are
         similar with and without demographic controls.

T3. Mean-reversion / ceiling effects that differ by grade and interact with
    new score scale.  
    Remedy:  
       • Replicate using raw IRT theta scores (where available) instead of
         percentile-ranks;  
       • Show robustness when excluding top/bottom 5 % of the distribution.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R CODE OUTLINE  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# -------------------------------------------------
# 0. packages
# -------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)     # fast high-dim fixed-effect regressions
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)

# -------------------------------------------------
# 1. data loading
# -------------------------------------------------
cms   <- fread("CMS_EOG_math_1999_2009.csv")   # student-level
piat  <- fread("NLSY79_child_PIAThistory.csv") # student-level

# -------------------------------------------------
# 2. variable construction – CMS
# -------------------------------------------------
cms[, post2001 := (year >= 2001)]
cms[, post2006 := (year >= 2006)]
cms[, upper     := fifelse(grade %in% 6:8, 1L, 0L)]

# proxy for latent knowledge
# long-run outcome (college) comes from clearinghouse; merge by student_id
college <- fread("CMS_clearinghouse_link.csv")
cms <- merge(cms, college, by = "student_id", all.x = TRUE)
cms[, college_attend := fifelse(is.na(college_enroll)==TRUE, 0L, 1L)]

# -------------------------------------------------
# 3. estimate knowledge-to-score slope β_gct
# -------------------------------------------------
# collapse to grade×cohort×edition cell
beta_est <- cms[
  , .(beta = coef(feols(scale(eog_math) ~ college_attend))[2]),
  by = .(grade, cohort = year - grade, edition_grp = fifelse(year<2001,0,
                                fifelse(year<2006,1,2)) )
]

# -------------------------------------------------
# 4. main DID: equation (1)
# -------------------------------------------------
# indicator that cell is after redesign event (0=pre-2001,1=2001-2005,2=post-2006)
beta_est[, post := (edition_grp>0)]
est <- feols(beta ~ post*upper | grade + edition_grp, data = beta_est, weights = ~N)

summary(est)

# -------------------------------------------------
# 5. robustness: triple-diff with reading placebo
# -------------------------------------------------
reading <- fread("CMS_EOG_reading_1999_2009.csv")
# similar steps to build beta_read
beta_read <- ...       # build as above for reading

# merge math & reading
both <- merge(beta_est[,.(grade,cohort,edition_grp,upper,beta_math=beta)],
              beta_read[,.(grade,cohort,beta_read=beta)], 
              by=c("grade","cohort"), all = TRUE)

both_long <- melt(both, id.vars = c("grade","cohort","edition_grp","upper"),
                  variable.name = "subject", value.name = "beta")

both_long[, math := (subject=="beta_math")]

triple <- feols(beta ~ post*upper*math | grade+edition_grp+subject,
                data = both_long, weights = ~N)
summary(triple)

# -------------------------------------------------
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. EXPECTED RESULTS  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
• If scaling artifacts are important, δ < 0: the post-redesign change will
  mechanically RAISE the measured payoff to knowledge in lower grades relative
  to upper grades (because the distribution has been re-compressed), partially
  erasing the previously observed pattern of small upper-grade effects.  
• Magnitude: I expect roughly one-third to one-half of the 0.20 sd gap in
  measured treatment effects between grades 4 and 8 documented in prior work
  to vanish after re-scaling.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (DID)  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: No differential pre-trends (event-study shows flat leads)........... 1  
C2: Correct functional form / linearity of trends........................ 1  
C3: No composition changes that correlate with treatment................. 0  
C4: No simultaneous interventions at the same cut-point.................. 0  
C5: Robust to alternative control groups (reading, PIAT sample).......... 1  

Total: 3 / 5 – satisfactory but requires careful robustness work.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
This plan uses exogenous shocks to the scaling of North Carolina’s EOG math
tests to causally isolate the “measurement width” component behind grade-level
and fade-out regularities.
